games.title: Language Choice
games.description: Choose the form that makes the unit language accurate.

rounds.prompt: Which machine would you use to heat a bowl of soup quickly?
rounds.explanation: A microwave is a machine that cooks or heats food quickly, so the soup is warm in minutes.

rounds.prompt: Which word names big machines that work together to do a heavy job?
rounds.explanation: Machinery names the big machines; cocoa is a powder, an attic is a room and a crew is a group of people.

rounds.prompt: Read this line from “The Attic Clue”: “They took torches, brooms, and a _____ to hold any papers they found.” Which word fits the gap?
rounds.explanation: Only a folder holds papers; the other three are vehicles or a viewing tool.

rounds.prompt: In “A Look at the Stars”, what can a telescope show you on the moon?
rounds.explanation: The text says you can see the craters on the moon and the rings around a planet.

rounds.prompt: Which sentence uses “have to” correctly?
choices: She have to clean the attic.
She has to clean the attic.
She has to cleaning the attic.
She have to cleaning the attic.
rounds.answer: She has to clean the attic.
rounds.explanation: After she we use has to, and the verb that follows stays in its base form: clean.

rounds.prompt: Which word correctly completes this sentence: “A crew is a group of people _____ work together.”?
rounds.explanation: We use who for people; which is for things, whose shows belonging and what is not a relative pronoun here.

games.title: Reading Detective
games.description: Use unit evidence to solve each reading clue.

rounds.prompt: Which tool does Amal use to join her homework pages together?
choices: Amal uses a stapler to join her homework pages together.
It means the telescope makes faraway things look near; the sky does not actually move.
They found drawings of machines and a note about building the future.
rounds.answer: Amal uses a stapler to join her homework pages together.
rounds.explanation: The second sentence of the text names the stapler as the tool for joining pages.

rounds.prompt: According to the text, what two jobs does heavy machinery do inside a factory?
choices: Metal must stay out because it can cause sparks.
They built a toy helicopter, and the plastic shield protected its wires.
Heavy machinery helps people build cars and lift boxes.
rounds.answer: Heavy machinery helps people build cars and lift boxes.
rounds.explanation: Both jobs sit in the same factory sentence, so give both building and lifting.

rounds.prompt: Why does the speaker warn you never to put metal inside the microwave?
choices: She learned that tools help us, but teamwork builds the best things of all.
Metal must stay out because it can cause sparks.
You have to stay close so that the food does not get too hot.
rounds.answer: Metal must stay out because it can cause sparks.
rounds.explanation: The warning and its reason are joined by because in the third sentence of the talk.

rounds.prompt: Who does the song thank at the end, and what do those people do?
choices: It thanks the people who work night and day to keep us safe.
You have to stay close so that the food does not get too hot.
She hoped a future student would use her drawings and invent something new.
rounds.answer: It thanks the people who work night and day to keep us safe.
rounds.explanation: The last line names the workers, not the machines, so the answer must be about people.

rounds.prompt: What did Amal and Leo find inside the briefcase in the attic?
choices: It thanks the people who work night and day to keep us safe.
Amal uses a stapler to join her homework pages together.
They found drawings of machines and a note about building the future.
rounds.answer: They found drawings of machines and a note about building the future.
rounds.explanation: The briefcase is opened one line after Amal points at it, and two things come out of it.

rounds.prompt: What does Amal say she has learned by the last line of the story?
choices: Heavy machinery helps people build cars and lift boxes.
She learned that tools help us, but teamwork builds the best things of all.
They had to wear gloves and masks because the attic might be dusty.
rounds.answer: She learned that tools help us, but teamwork builds the best things of all.
rounds.explanation: The closing line is Amal's own words, so the answer should quote or closely follow them.

games.title: Question Quest
games.description: Read each unit question carefully and choose the best answer.

rounds.prompt: Which word correctly completes this sentence: “A crew is a group of people _____ work together.”?
rounds.explanation: We use who for people; which is for things, whose shows belonging and what is not a relative pronoun here.

rounds.prompt: Which sentence is written as an imperative instruction?
choices: The hands are washed by me.
I washed my hands before dinner.
Wash your hands before you eat.
rounds.answer: Wash your hands before you eat.
rounds.explanation: An imperative starts with the base verb and needs no subject, so only the last sentence gives an instruction.

rounds.prompt: Read this line from “The Attic Clue”: “It had buttons and even a tiny _____ made of plastic.” Which word fits the gap?
rounds.explanation: The toy helicopter's shield was the flat guard that protected its wires from harm.

rounds.prompt: Which word completes the safety rule from the microwave talk: “Stir the food with a clean _____ before you eat.”?
rounds.explanation: The talk asks you to stir with a clean utensil, and a spoon or fork is exactly that.

rounds.prompt: Which sentence uses the past simple correctly?
choices: She goed to the market last week.
She went to the market last week.
She go to the market last week.
She will went to the market last week.
rounds.answer: She went to the market last week.
rounds.explanation: Go is irregular, so its past simple form is went, and will never stands beside a past verb.

rounds.prompt: Which machine would you use to heat a bowl of soup quickly?
rounds.explanation: A microwave is a machine that cooks or heats food quickly, so the soup is warm in minutes.
